title: This Travel-Ready Hoodie Is The Best Thing I’ve Bought All Year
text:
This Travel-Ready Hoodie Is The Best Thing I’ve Bought All Year

I can’t tell you how many social media ads I scroll past on any given day. However, I can tell you that the stars must have aligned (or fine, my algorithm reflected a love of naps, kittens, and other cozy things) to unite me with Comfrt, specifically the brand’s now internet-famous Airplane Mode Travel Hoodie.

When I tell you that a truer match couldn’t be conjured in heaven, I’m barely exaggerating. The moment I saw Comfrt’s hoodie with a built-in eye mask, my thumb and heart both stopped. The next thing I knew, I’d hit “place order” on matching sweatshirts for me and my husband.

That was back in February, and over five months later, the Comfrt Airplane Mode Travel Hoodie is still among my most-worn items in my closet. (In my mind, it’s more than paid for itself in terms of how many times I wear it.) Keep reading for why I’m already calling it one of the smartest purchases of the year, and why it belongs in your closet.

But unique features aside, it’s a really well-made sweatshirt. It’s constructed from a sturdy yet soft cotton-polyester fabric that doesn’t look bulky. I got it in the Steel Grey colorway, which feels neutral but not boring. I usually wear an XS (the size ranges from XS to 3X), and IMO, this has a slightly oversized fit that I love. It’s become the first thing I pack when I’m going on a trip, and when I’m home? I wear it when I need a quick power nap and am asleep within minutes (according to my Oura ring). And if you’re out and about running errands, just tuck the eye mask into the hood or wear the hood as you would normally with any other hoodie. (And in case you’re wondering, yes, Comfrt makes “regular” sweatshirts, along with other athleisure basics, travel bags, and accessories, and randomly, blankets.)

Whenever I post about this hoodie on my own Instagram, a handful of friends always pop up in my DMs to express their delight and/or tell me I inspired their purchase. (“Omg is that eye mask attached to the hoodie?!! I need that,” shared one friend, followed by a screenshot of her subsequent order.) Comfrt’s signature hoodie retails for $140, but is currently on sale for $59 — my advice for tired travelers and sleep enthusiasts everywhere: Don’t miss out on making this very special sweatshirt yours.

title: The Handbag Trend That Effortlessly Transitions From Summer To Fall
text:
The Handbag Trend That Effortlessly Transitions From Summer To Fall
Fashion is far from that post-pandemic dopamine dressing bubble, and it’s also emerging from a sweeping beige wave and quiet luxury spell. It’s certainly not dead, celebrity stylist Gabriella Karefa-Johnson tells Refinery29, “but the appetite for texture and pattern is definitely back, and snakeskin certainly has a starring role to play.” Fashion feels like it’s returning to a more whimsical, expressive self. We’ve seen this everywhere from street style in Paris to some of our favorite looks at the 2026 ESSENCE Festival of Culture. It makes sense that snakeskin bags are coming back into focus, too.

We’ve seen them everywhere, from Lupita Nyong'o carrying Brahmin on the Odyssey press tour to Khaite’s runway show in New York. Whether in a natural hue or a brighter, more artificial colorway, snake print adds something bold to any look, whether you’re headed to brunch or carrying it as your daily work bag. As Karefa-Johnson, who’s Depop’s Trend Spokesperson, says, “what I think is actually happening is people are just wanting to be loud and a bit messy again. Snakeskin gives you texture and a bit of wildness without committing to anything too extra.”

It helps that there’s been a crocodile bag wave since the spring, in large part to Chanel Creative Director Matthieu Blazy’s “Chanelmania” that descended when his debut collection hit store shelves. One of its stars? The reptilian-touched tote bags that went viral. (Karefa-Johnson herself bought the minty “mock-croc” shopping tote.) “Once something like that bag becomes the whole industry's obsession, everyone starts noticing animal prints and textures again, even outside of Chanel entirely,” the stylist, who’s worked with everyone from Bella Hadid to Vice President Kamala Harris, tells Refinery29.

If wearing snakeskin feels new or daring, style it as if it’s a neutral. As Karefa-Johnson says, “snakeskin actually plays really well with denim, T-shirts, and simple shapes because its texture is already doing a lot of work. Your outfit doesn't need to compete with it.” 

For anyone looking to score genuine snakeskin handbags without sticker shock, she shouts out Depop. “[It’s] a great place to source true vintage. You can find real snakeskin from the ’90s and early 2000s, which hit different than a lot of what's being made new right now. The leather is usually better, and it’s often available at a more affordable price point,” the stylist adds.

Ahead, we’ve rounded up our 11 favorite snakeskin bags o satisfy your craving and carry all summer long. The best part? There’s a range of styles and price points, with plenty that’ll work year-round and others that’ll be a star in your summer wardrobe.

title: The Official Summer Uniform Is Fun Pants & Basic Tops
text:
The Official Summer Uniform Is Fun Pants & Basic Tops

Forget simple jeans and “going-out tops”. Funky pants and basic tops might just be this summer’s chicest fashion formula.

Sometimes getting dressed is all about finding the right fashion formula. Every season brings a new trend, and this summer, it all comes down to funky pants. All summer, I couldn’t stop thinking about owning a pair of blue, yellow, and white striped pants. I wasn’t looking for a specific brand. I had simply imagined how good they would look with a tank top. That’s when I realized that I might have found this season’s ultimate outfit formula.

The thing about fashion is that it can make you crave something you never knew you wanted. And sometimes, that one unexpected piece ends up reflecting more about your own style than anything already hanging in your closet. 

Long before fun pants took over this season, there was sleepwear-inspired dressing. Over time, the pajama pants trend evolved into the colorful, expressive styles that we’re seeing today, in which bold prints, vibrant colors, playful silhouettes, and unexpected textures take center stage. Dolce & Gabbana’s Spring/Summer 2026 collection featured blue striped pajama-inspired trousers with embellishmed details, while Versace‘s Spring/Summer 2026 drop embraced bold blue, yellow, and orange striped pants with an ’80s-inspired feeling. And then suddenly, statement pants were not just for the bedroom, the beach, or the runways anymore. 

Live, Laugh, Love Fun Pants!

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Millie Bobby Brown (@milliebobbybrown)

This summer, statement pants are paired with the most understated tops, proving that sometimes one great piece is enough. A tank top, a baby tee, an oversized button-down shirt, or a bodysuit is all you need for styling, as inspired by Millie Bobby Brown, who paired Pamela Anderson’s archival embellished jeans with a fitted white baby tee, or Hailey Bieber, who paired bold polka-dot capris with a black boatneck top.

Celebrity and editorial stylist Lauren Croft told IMAGE that she’s “really drawn to those one-off eccentric pieces that are something different, and wearing that one statement piece that sets the tone for the whole outfit.” That’s exactly the role that fun pants have taken on this season. They will do all of the talking and can be the one unchangeable part of your style equation.

The best part? There are no rules. Animal print, sheer fabrics, embroidery, studs, bold colors, stripes, sequins, balloon silhouettes, barrel legs, or pajama-inspired styles all unite under the fun-pants umbrella. The only requirement is to have fun with them.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Leandra Medine Cohen (@leandramcohen)

During the day, style statement pants with a simple white crew-neck baby tee, flip-flops or ballet flats for coffee dates, lunch in the city, or summer vacations. When the sun goes down, you can switch the tee for a black satin strappy backless blouse, swap your flats for sleek heels or mules, layer on chunky jewelry, and the very same pants are instantly ready for dinner, rooftop drinks, or a summer party. For more styling inspiration, we can channel our inner Zara Larsson with bold-print trousers, a rhinestone bikini top or tied button-down shirt, and nostalgic accessories like statement sunglasses, skinny belts, and metallic kitten heels.

Personally, I’ve been reaching for my Lioness Penny Pants all summer long. The button-front detail running from the waist to the hem gives them (and me) plenty of personality. The simplicity of a basic top and minimalist jewelry let the pants shine. I’m also a fan of trousers long enough to cover my stilettos. They instantly make the silhouette feel sleeker, cooler, and bolder. 

So if you’re looking to refresh your wardrobe this summer, start with the pants, especially the funky ones.

title: This Pedicure Is Controversial, But I Wear It Every Spring & Summer
text:
This Pedicure Is Controversial, But I Wear It Every Spring & Summer

I’ve always loved a French pedicure. No matter what’s going on in my life, it always makes me feel polished, like I have my life together — even when I’m not wearing a lick of makeup, or I haven’t washed my hair in days. 

With that in mind, I’m thrilled that the design is making a comeback. But it’s not in the Y2K way you might remember from your teenage years (alongside velour tracksuits and frosted lip gloss). If Instagram is anything to go by, the French pedicure is chic and modern.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Harriet Westmoreland (@harrietwestmoreland)

What is a French pedicure? 

If you’re looking for a do-it-all pedicure that goes with everything and works for any occasion, the classic French is versatile. Whether you’re heading to the beach, the office, or your third wedding of the summer, it just works. Whether you love it or hate it, a French pedicure is a classic for a reason: “It’s clean, elegant, and endlessly wearable,” says Juanita Huber-Millet, founder and creative director of Townhouse. “Traditionally, this look features a soft nude or pink base with a crisp white tip.” Adding, “It’s that timeless contrast that makes it so instantly loved and recognizable.”

It’s little wonder, then, that the design is often spotted on some of the world’s biggest celebrities at red carpet events. Think Rihanna, Kylie Jenner, and Lily Allen, who are just a few stars frequently photographed with a fresh French pedicure. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Milly Mason (@millymason_)

What are the benefits of a French pedicure?

French pedicures aren’t limited to just pink and white; there are endless possibilities to explore with colors and creative designs: “French pedicures are back but in a unique and modern way,” says Fatima Naveed, senior brand manager at Duck & Dry. “We’re enjoying using fresh new shades and details to breathe new life into the traditional design,” like chrome and pastel tips, and jelly base colors.

Huber-Millet loves that the French pedicure complements every skin tone — and grows out beautifully. “It’s understated luxury that never goes out of style,” she says.

Why is the French pedicure considered controversial? 

But not everyone is sold on the French pedicure. If social media is anything to go by, it’s even a little controversial at times. Why? Naveed explains that the trend essentially emphasizes the overgrown tips of toenails, making critics question the look’s practicality. “Personally, though, I think that the key lies in the length as well as the choice of tip and base color,” she says. “A milky white or a sheer pink tip will give a more subtle, chic finish than bold white tips.” As for the base shade? “It’s more than just a background color; it sets the entire tone of the design.”

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Milly Mason (@millymason_)

What does the French pedicure look like in 2025? 

If you want to avoid the overgrown look, consider one of the biggest French pedicure trends. Enter: micro tips. “The micro French pedicure is gaining huge popularity,” says Naveed. “It consists of a very thin tip along the edge of toenails, which provides a clean and understated look.” The secret to pulling it off is keeping toenails short and well-groomed. This helps enhance the minimalist effect. Naveed’s clients also opt for a ‘Frombré’ effect (French ombré), which blends the nude base and milky white tip shades to lend a subtle, modern take on the look.

Huber-Millet adds that 2025 is seeing a real evolution of the French pedicure: “It’s all about tonal or unexpected color pairings, and playful accents like chrome, shimmer, or deep red shades for a moodier take. It’s fresh, flattering, and very now.”

Keeping that in mind, scroll on for nine French pedicure trends to try now.

title: 12 Fresh Bob Haircut Trends We’re Seeing Everywhere This Summer
text:
12 Fresh Bob Haircut Trends We’re Seeing Everywhere This Summer

When it comes to haircut trends, the choice is overwhelming, but if we had to crown one cut the current style du jour, it would be the bob. 

Its versatility is what gives the bob an edge over other cuts. Want to go really short? Consider the bixie, aka bob-meets-pixie. Worried about losing too much length? Try the lob, or long bob. That’s just the tip of the iceberg, because hairstylists from London to Los Angeles are dreaming up new iterations of the cut daily — and we predict that, this summer, there’ll be no escaping the temptation to brave the scissors.

With that in mind, scroll ahead for the bob haircut trends top stylists predict will reign supreme this summer and beyond.

DashDividers_1_500x100

The Korean Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Timothy Ting (@timothyting_hove)

Hairstylist George Curran bills the Korean bob as one of the most exciting haircut innovations. “The cut is designed so you can have a bob when your hair is tied or clipped up, and long hair when it’s worn down,” says Curren. It’s literally two hairstyles in one. “No extensions and all without committing to losing your length,” adds Curran. “It’s a clever optical illusion haircut using a specialist Korean cutting technique, and it’s perfect for anyone who wants versatility without compromise.” This video posted to Instagram by Timothy Ting is mesmerizing.

The Airy Bixie

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Jordz (@boyjordz.hair)

“This blends charm and delicacy with a modern and lived-in edge,” says Devin Graciano is a professional hairstylist and CEO of Goldie Locks. She adds, “The style is lightweight, soft, and full of movement, which gives it that effortless, airy feel,” — but it boasts attitude and intention, too. “The bixie complements the playful and confident person who wears it,” says Graciano. “It’s a cut that feels both current and timeless, with room for personalization depending on texture and personality.” This cut by Jordz is perfect. 

The Blunt Curly Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Nadine Koca | Fashion & Hair (@nadinekoca)

Curly hair specialist Dusty Schlabach predicts that the blunt curly bob will be everywhere. “It’s a zero-layer, ultra-clean blunt bob that sits right at the chin,” says Schlabach, adding, “It’s perfect for medium to low-density curls because it keeps the shape sleek without stacking or creating that Christmas tree effect at the baseline” — no triangular shapes here. Instead, the silhouette is “intentional,” says Schlabach, who suggests asking your stylist to cut your curls dry, exactly in their natural pattern. “Think a straight-across blunt line and no layers — just the slightest, almost invisible A-line so it sits clean at the chin,” says Schlabach. This cut on Nadine Koca is beautiful.

The Shattered Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Pam Mlunjwana (@pammacb)

Rather than a clean, blunt line, the ends of the shattered bob are point-cut or “shattered” by slicing into the hair vertically to create a “choppy, airy, slightly fragmented finish,” says Curran, like this look on Pam Mlunjwana. “It has that effortless, undone vibe,” he continues. But make no mistake: “It’s a very technical cut that relies on precision and the right styling products.” Layering is essential to add movement, says Curran. “You want the hair to have body and flow, without slipping into that helmet-like shape. I remove a lot of weight through the layers, particularly around the [back], which gives the cut bounce and stops it feeling heavy or bulky.”

Curran says the shattered bob looks best when it’s relaxed and a little tousled. “That cool-girl, lived-in texture feels intentional but never overdone. A product like Tecni Art Pli works really well, and finishing with Techni Art Volume Dust.”

The Bangless French Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Faick Zekai (@faick_hair)

When Curran thinks of a French bob, the words classic, timeless, and iconic spring to his mind. “In 2025, we saw this style evolve with softer layering around the face,” he says. “But as we head into 2026, it’s all about a more grown-out, effortless version of the look,” like this one by Faick Zekai. According to Curran, it stays sophisticated thanks to a strong, heavy finish through the ends and very minimal layering throughout.

The Liquid Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by TAMPA HAIRSTYLIST (@sophie.coastalhair)

Coined by Graciano, the liquid bob is a “sleek, softly sculpted bob with seamless layers and polished ends that move like fluid.” It’s glossy, weightless, and intentionally refined, she adds. Simply ask your stylist for a “blunt-to-soft perimeter bob,” advises Graciano, complete with subtle internal layering. “Wearing it blow-dried smooth emphasizes shine and swing,” says Graciano. This cut by Tampa hairstylist Sophie is stunning.

The Rounded Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Yasmeen ياسمين (@yasmeenscott)

According to Schlabach, the rounded layered curly bob — as seen here on Yasmeen Scott — is the total opposite of the aforementioned blunt bob. “This cut uses soft, intentional layers to create a rounder, more lifted shape that distributes weight evenly,” says Schlabach. “It’s ideal for dense curls that tend to build bulk at the bottom because the layers prevent heaviness and open up movement throughout the shape.”

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Ashlynn Rudzinski (@arud_)

It looks just as great on straight and wavy hair, as shown by Ashlynn Rudzinski here. So what should you ask for? “A rounded bob with intentional layering to release weight and build shape — cut dry so the layers match the natural curl pattern and keep the silhouette lifted,” says Schlabach.

The Cowgirl Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by miho mai / 福岡ボブ / ボブ / ボブパーマ / 福岡美容室 / ナチュラル (@zoey__mai)

The cowgirl bob has a strong ’90s influence, says Curran. “I think it’s going to be a big evolution from the French bob or the blunt, one-length, ultra-polished look à la Sofia Richie-Grainge,” he adds. The cowgirl bob has a few defining attributes: “It’s softer, shaggier, and more relaxed — for those who don’t want a super-sleek finish and prefer a bit more movement and natural texture.” Curran points to Alexa Chung as inspiration. “What I love most is how bespoke you can make it,” adds Curran. “You can tailor it completely to the client and frame the face with soft or grown-out bangs.”

To style it, Curran recommends using a curling iron to create a subtle kick through the ends. “This will enhance that relaxed, cowgirl-inspired movement,” he says. “I always finish with L’Oréal Professionnel Tecni Art Volume Panache to keep the texture airy and full of body. You want it to look deliberately imperfect.” Miho Mai gets it so right here.

The Soft Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Faick Zekai (@faick_hair)

This is a rounded, gently layered bob, which Graciano says is designed to enhance natural texture. “It keeps the shape airy and controlled, never bulky,” she says — just like this cut by Faick Zekai. “Ask your stylist for a bob that hits between the jaw and collarbone, with light internal layering and curl-by-curl shaping to maintain softness and movement.”

The Asymmetric Pixie Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Sheridan Holyoak (@shmoakin_hair)

Brace yourselves: the pob, aka the pixie bob, is making a comeback — and Curran predicts it’ll be one of the standout cuts of 2026. “Think Scarlett Johansson circa 2015 or Victoria Beckham in her 2007 Posh bob era,” says Curran. He adds, “We’re seeing a real shift towards shapes that feel more architectural yet still wearable, and this cut ticks every box. I love the contrast it creates: one side sharp and cropped, the other slightly longer, sweeping, and sculpted.” Even better, Curran says it’s the ideal next step for anyone with a ’90s bob who wants to go shorter. “It’s bold, low-maintenance, and super stylish.” We adore this cut by Sheridan Holyoak. 

The Curly Lob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Jessenia Robayo (@jesseniaspallet)

Schlabach says that the curly lob, or long bob, is a slightly longer version of the rounded and blunt curly bobs. “It’s a shoulder-grazing cut that keeps length while maintaining structure,” adds Schlabach, “and it’s often paired with thoughtful face-framing or a soft veil bang to open up the front and create natural movement.” Thanks to the additional few inches, this style works well across most curl types and densities, says Schlabach. Remember to request some movement around the face to give it dimension, like this cut by Jessenia Robayo.

The Layered Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by miho mai / 福岡ボブ / ボブ / ボブパーマ / 福岡美容室 / ナチュラル (@zoey__mai)

Curran says the layered bob was one of the most-liked bob haircuts on TikTok last month. “It’s a longer, ’90s-inspired style with layers at the front and throughout,” much like this cut by Miho Mai. The slightly wet-look texture emphasizes the choppiness of the layers, giving it a modern feel, while the lash-grazing full fringe brings in a touch of retro balance.

title: All You Need To Know About BIAB — & How It Could Help Grow Your Natural Nails
text:
All You Need To Know About BIAB — & How It Could Help Grow Your Natural Nails

As a beauty editor, it’s my job to test beauty treatments, but there are only a handful that I’m really obsessed with. Sure, there are tons of interesting options out there, like LED facials and injectable moisturizer, but few are genuinely innovative and game-changing (in my opinion, the single most overused phrase in the beauty industry).  

Without a doubt, one of those innovations and my can’t-live-without product is builder in a bottle, which you may also know as BIAB nails. I’ll even bet money on you trying it and loving it. Here’s everything you need to know about the new nail treatment sweeping salons everywhere. 

What are BIAB nails?  

BIAB (also known as builder gel) was developed by the brand The Gel Bottle. Creative nail expert and content creator, Sadie Jordan, always uses BIAB on her clients: “It’s a [curable] gel nail enhancement designed to add strength and structure to your natural nails, helping them to grow out without breaking as easily,” says Jordan. She adds that BIAB is more viscous than gel polish. “It allows you to build an apex — the highest part of a nail enhancement, most visible from the side angle — which is what makes your nail more durable.”  

BIAB is layered on top of your natural nail (whatever the length) to lend strength and prevent breakage. BIAB comes in a range of different colors, but the most popular tends to be clear or neutral pink. It can be used as a base coat (with gel polish layered over the top, including nail art) or applied on its own.  

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The GelBottle Inc™ (@the_gelbottle_inc)

What are the benefits of BIAB nails?  

The main benefit of BIAB is the ability to grow your natural nails underneath. Even long-term nail-biters, or those whose nails are prone to breakage, tend to have success with growth. What’s more, countless BIAB nail looks can be achieved without glue or plastic tips, says Jordan. This means you can have long-lasting manicures with a similar removal process to regular gel by simply filing away the top layer and soaking off the product with acetone. 

Another benefit of BIAB is that it can be used alongside nail forms (a paper or foil tip) to repair chipped corners. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The GelBottle Inc™ (@the_gelbottle_inc)

What’s the difference between BIAB nails, traditional gel, Gel-X nails, and acrylics?  

It can be hard to tell, but there are differences between BIAB, traditional gel, Gel-X, and acrylics.

Gel nail polish was developed by CND under the brand name Shellac and is a liquid polish that is cured and hardened under a UV lamp. Curing makes gel polish chip-resistant and gives it a longer wear.  

BIAB is a form of gel polish that has a stronger base — this is why it assists growth. An upside of BIAB is that it can be soaked off just like gel polish. Both gel polish and BIAB give that incredible, long-lasting shine that regular nail polish can’t achieve. 

Gel-X is a gel nail extension system developed by Aprés Nails, where full-cover tips are bonded to the natural nail with gel and cured under a UV lamp, then shaped to your preference. BIAB doesn’t require tips. Instead, it’s applied onto the natural nail.  

Acrylics are created using liquid monomer and powder polymer, which should be mixed carefully by your nail tech. Acrylics don’t need curing under a lamp and harden within a few minutes. If you’re someone who loves really long nails, acrylics tend to be a sturdier option. One similarity between BIAB and acrylics is that once the nail starts to grow out, you can get an infill (where product is applied to the nail growth area).  

So what’s the best technique? It all depends on your budget, what your nail tech offers, the outcome and length you’re looking for, as well as your activity level, or how much you use your hands. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The GelBottle Inc™ (@the_gelbottle_inc)

How long do BIAB nails last? 

Luxury nail artist and beauty professional Charlotte Emily explains that most of her clients come in every three weeks to maintain their BIAB nails. But she notes that if there’s proper nail prep, a BIAB set can last for much longer. That said, keeping BIAB nails on for longer than four weeks isn’t recommended, as lifting can allow water to get trapped beneath the gel and encourage bacterial growth. After three or four weeks, BIAB nails can either be infilled or soaked off.  

Is there anyone who shouldn’t have BIAB nails? 

Both Emily and Jordan note that those with extremely damaged nails (for example, very thin, extremely brittle, and lifting away from the nail bed) shouldn’t get BIAB nails. In some cases, those with conditions like psoriasis may also want to avoid BIAB nails. “Applying BIAB directly to a severely damaged nail bed can cause heat spikes — a stinging sensation on the nail bed — and the product should not come into contact with skin,” says Jordan.  

A qualified nail tech will let you know whether you’re a suitable candidate for BIAB and can create a treatment plan that’s best suited to your nails. Happily, Emily said she’s never had to turn anyone away from BIAB nails.  

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The GelBottle Inc™ (@the_gelbottle_inc)

Are there any downsides to BIAB nails? 

“BIAB does take a little longer to soak off compared to gel polish,” says Jordan, but as long as the top coat is filed and broken down, this isn’t a major issue. “It can also make your nails grow out very fast,” she adds, “so you may need to have manicures more frequently if you don’t like the look of regrowth.”  

At present, BIAB has no downsides for Emily. “My clients and I are happy with the results, and it has created a low-maintenance manicure which is great for a busy lifestyle,” she says.   

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The GelBottle Inc™ (@the_gelbottle_inc)

Where can you get BIAB nails, and how much do BIAB nails cost?  

Today, BIAB is just as widely available as gel polish — if you’re unsure, simply call your local nail salon and ask specifically for the treatment.  

The cost of nails always depends on where you live, with cities being the most expensive. In New York and LA, for example, a typical price range for basic BIAB is between $40 to $80.

title: Tom Holland: Zendaya Is “More Talented Than I Am”
text:
Tom Holland: Zendaya Is “More Talented Than I Am”

If you’re looking for more confirmation that Tom Holland and Zendaya are Hollywood’s reigning power couple, the Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour is proof that the duo are not only the (short) king and (style) queen of the moment, they are also madly in love. The married couple have taken over our timelines with adorable quips and quotes about each other, but this latest admission from Holland may just be my personal favorite. 

While walking the red carpet at the Los Angeles premiere of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Holland gushed about working with Zendaya over the decade that they have been playing MJ and Peter Parker in the Marvel franchise. “ I’m so grateful with how this has all ended up — professionally and personally,” Holland said. “I wouldn’t want anything to change. Where I’m standing here today, I feel so blessed and lucky to get to do what I do on the stage that I do it on, with the wonderful people that I get to share that experience with.” 

And when asked by Refinery29 reporter Dawnie Jefferson what the best part of working with one of those wonderful people — his wife — is, Holland said, “That she is more talented than I am, and she makes everyone in their scenes way, way better. That’s the best thing about working with Z.” 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Refinery29 (@refinery29)

I just want to say that to my fellow #Tomdaya day ones, we used to pray for moments like this. When we were in those Tumblr fanfic streets (just me?), who would have imagined this happy ending for our faves? It’s me. I imagined it. But I digress. This answer outranks some of the couple’s most viral moments (real ones know the famous giggly “avocados” junket clip) for me because it encapsulates the love and respect Holland has for his wife, professionally, not just personally.

My wish for all straight women is to get you a man who speaks so highly of you and your work, a man who loves you so loudly he’s unafraid to say you are better at things than him. Sure, the bar is on the floor thanks to incel culture and the men we’ve lost to the manosphere, but REAL men like Holland know that husbands are supposed to be down bad for their wives and shout that fact from the rooftops whenever possible. Ladies, never forget that’s the kind of love we all deserve! 

Holland and Zendaya (it’s a good thing she goes by one name because we don’t know what her legal last name is these days) were 20 and 19 years-old respectively when their first Spider-Man movie, Spider-Man: Homecoming was released. A decade later (Holland just turned 30), the pair are married (both Holland and Zendaya’s stylist Law Roach have confirmed the nuptials) and open about how thankful they are to be on this journey together. The couple also just starred in the biggest movie in the world, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, together. And if Spider-Man: Brand New Day achieves its projected box office numbers, they might make Hollywood power couple history as the first married couple to star in the #1 and #2 movies in the world at the same time. Turns out, the greatest Spider-Man love story wasn’t Peter and MJ — it was the one happening between takes.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is in theatres this Friday, July 31.

title: We Tried Every New e.l.f. Hair Product — & These Are The Ones Worth Buying
text:
We Tried Every New e.l.f. Hair Product — & These Are The Ones Worth Buying

We’re big fans of e.l.f. Cosmetics here at Refinery29. Among our all-time favorites are the Halo Glow Skin Tint (which has picked up not one but two R29 beauty awards), the $6 Liquid Metallic Eyeshadow that I wore on my wedding day, the viral Power Grip Primer that outperforms my expensive ones, and plenty of other affordable standouts. Now, that list is about to get even more crowded, thanks to the brand’s first foray into haircare.

Inspired by prestige formulas — but made with e.l.f.’s signature budget-friendly pricing in mind — the debut collection features everything from wash-day essentials like shampoos and conditioners to glossing treatments and styling products, with every item priced under $10. Naturally, we had to put the range to the test to see if it could deliver salon-worthy results without the expensive markup.

Ahead, find our honest reviews of the standout products worth adding to your routine ASAP.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Never Thirsty Moisturizing Shampoo, $9

“I have a lot of hair, but it’s fine, so I took one look at the name of this shampoo and assumed it wasn’t for me — until I tried it. I’ve never known a shampoo to lather up as quickly — and clean as effectively — as this one. Even when my hair is particularly dirty or loaded with product from previous days, a small squeeze creates rich suds that slice through grease and buildup, leaving my scalp and lengths feeling clean but never stripped.

Those with sensitive or reactive scalps will be pleased to know that it’s sulfate-free, but there are still a handful of excellent, gentle surfactants that create the bubbles, including sodium C14-16 olefin sulfonate and sodium lauroyl methyl isethionate, so you can be confident it’s lifting away as much debris as possible. I’m convinced the addition of argan oil, a deeply moisturizing ingredient, helps make my hair look shinier, feel softer, and leaves split ends looking less noticeable.” — Jacqueline Kilikita, Beauty Director

“I’m really not snobby when it comes to shampoo. Don’t get me wrong — luxury formulas are a treat to use — but in my experience, drugstore shampoos get the job done just as well. I’d rather splurge on products that stay on my hair for longer than a few minutes. That said, I’m convinced Never Thirsty Shampoo is a prestige formula masquerading as an affordable gem. It has a fresh, lightly floral scent that isn’t overly sweet, and, as Jackie mentioned, it leaves my hair feeling thoroughly clean without stripping away moisture. The sulfate-free formula lathers beautifully, while its hydrating ingredients help keep my hair soft instead of squeaky. Paired with the conditioner, it’s the perfect duo for hair that feels clean, hydrated, and noticeably silkier.”— Karina Hoshikawa, Senior Writer

“With low-porosity hair that takes a long time to absorb water, I’m used to spending at least five minutes under the shower head before my strands even feel wet. Because of that initial water barrier, building up a lather usually takes a little extra effort, and that was the case here. What immediately stood out, though, was the very gentle, barely-there scent—perfect if you prefer a subtle fragrance in the shower. But the real surprise came at the rinse: after just one lather, my hair felt unbelievably soft before I’d even touched the conditioner.” — Alexis Bennett Parker, Shopping Director

DashDividers_1_500x100

Never Thirsty Moisturizing Conditioner, $9

“This hair-washing duo simply isn’t complete without the conditioner, which might just be my favorite product in the range (don’t tell the shampoo). Though it’s packed with shine-enhancing argan oil and strand-strengthening proteins, it’s surprisingly lightweight, slipping easily through the hair so you can coat every strand. Better still, it rinses out quickly and cleanly, unlike some ‘moisturizing’ conditioners that cling on and leave hair feeling greasy when you’re blow-drying (the worst). I’ve been using it consistently alongside the shampoo since it landed on my desk, and the compliments on how full and bouncy my hair looks (including one from Karina!) have been rolling in. At just $9, I’ll definitely be stockpiling it once I run out.” — Jacqueline Kilikita, Beauty Director

“I may not be particularly picky when it comes to shampoo, but I definitely am when it comes to conditioner. I have thick, frizz-prone hair, so if a conditioner isn’t moisturizing enough, it’s an express ticket to Pooftown, USA. It’s a bit of a ‘Three Bears’ situation: Formulas that are too light don’t do enough for my hair, while ones that are too rich leave it looking limp and greasy. Never Thirsty Conditioner, like Goldilocks’ favorite porridge, is just right — it has plenty of slip, rinses away clean without any residue, and leaves my hair looking smooth, shiny, and hydrated after air-drying. Consider me impressed.” — Karina Hoshikawa, Senior Writer

“Because I typically dedicate an entire day to wash day, I wish the packaging offered clearer guidance on leave-in time; on a weekend, I easily could have left this on under a cap for hours. Testing this on a busy weekday meant I only had a few minutes to spare while showering, but it still laid down a deeply hydrated foundation. I noticed the subtle scent picked up a bit more here than with the shampoo, leaving a fresh, clean hint of fragrance as it worked its magic.” — Alexis Bennett Parker, Shopping Director

DashDividers_1_500x100

Humidity Hero Anti-Frizz Styling Spray, $9

“As someone with kinky-curly hair who loves wearing it straight in the summer, this is an absolute holy grail. After washing, I made sure my hair was completely saturated from roots to ends before blow-drying with tension to lock in the treatment. I went into flat-ironing thinking I’d skipped heat protectant in the name of testing, only to realize this heat-activated formula actually has built-in heat protection. The finish was so glass-like, silky, and glossy that my natural hair honestly looked better than my extensions. It sealed my low-porosity strands so completely that humidity didn’t stand a chance.” — Alexis Bennett Parker, Shopping Director

“Even before I tried a drop of this stuff, I immediately thought, ‘Is this a dupe for Color Wow Dream Coat?’ based on the packaging alone. Like Dream Coat, Humidity Hero is a lightweight, heat-activated smoothing treatment designed to smooth hair, even lasting through up to three shampoos. After spraying liberally (which I feel less guilty about doing when one bottle is just $9), I blow- dry with tension (with a brush and blow dryer, or the Shark FlexFusion), then I go through each section drying the hair. After I’m done with my whole head, my hair immediately feels super sleek and smooth, but the true test was seeing how it lasted through a whole weekend in Austin, Texas. While it didn’t eliminate all frizz and flyaways (nearly impossible, when you have as much hair as I do), it definitely helped a lot given how humid the weather was.” — Karina Hoshikawa, Senior Writer

DashDividers_1_500x100

3-in-Wonder Magic Styling Cream, $9

“To wrap up the look, I reached for a tiny, pea-sized amount of the cream formula to tame the shorter pieces and new growth along my part line. Literally the smallest dab was able to instantly lay down those stubborn flyaways without flattening my hair or leaving a tacky residue. It keeps everything laid, smooth, and polished while allowing your press to maintain all its natural bounce.” — Alexis Bennett Parker, Shopping Director

DashDividers_1_500x100

Gloss Mode Treatment Oil, $10

“I know I’ve found a truly great hair product when I can’t stop touching my hair after using it. That’s exactly what happened with e.l.f.’s new haircare range, but especially Gloss Mode. I’ve tried more hair oils than I can count; it’s one of the few product categories that has earned a permanent spot in my otherwise low-maintenance routine. Unlike featherweight oils like K18’s and Bumble and bumble’s (two of my longtime favorites), Gloss Mode feels more like an oil-serum hybrid, with a plush, cushiony texture that smooths and softens without feeling greasy. I like to work a few drops through my lengths on freshly washed hair before letting it air-dry. It leaves my hair feeling silky, glossy, and smelling incredible. I get hints of vanilla and warm musk, personally. It feels every bit as indulgent as a luxury formula, yet it costs just $10.” — Karina Hoshikawa, Senior Writer

“Even though my silk press already had incredible shine, I had to give this a try. The slow-pouring dropper is a total lifesaver; you never have to worry about accidentally overdoing it or weighing down your hair. I dispersed four drops in my palms and smoothed it over the top of my hair, and it added a stunning, high-glow radiance without feeling greasy or heavy. It’s ultra-lightweight, silky, and gives you that perfect salon-quality finish.” — Alexis Bennett Parker, Shopping Director

“I didn’t think anything would be good enough to rival my trusty Kérastase Huile Ultime (I’ve been using it for at least five years), but this just might. I know it looks suspiciously similar to Olaplex’s No.7 Bonding Oil, but the texture (velvety yet lightweight) and the results (shine, softness, fewer visible split ends, and less frizz) are so comparable to Huile Ultime that I had to double-check I hadn’t gone on autopilot and used that instead. I apply three or four drops to damp hair, raking it through my mid-lengths and ends before rough-drying, and immediately — even without intense heat from tongs or straighteners — my hair feels silky and has an impressive shine. I love that it’s housed in a nifty, purse-friendly bottle, so I pop it in my bag for touch-ups if needed.” — Jacqueline Kilikita, Beauty Director

DashDividers_1_500x100

3-in-Wonder Magic Styling Cream Wand, $6

“I love hair-taming wands, especially when I’m wearing my hair in a slicked-back bun, but most are gels that harden on strands and eventually flake off throughout the day. Not this one. It’s a hydrating, moisturizing cream instead, so it sinks into strands rather than sitting on top like a lacquer. I have baby hairs that I like to essentially glue down, and this lets me do that without feeling like my scalp is frozen in place. It’s also great for keeping frizzy and flyaway strands on lockdown. I’ve never used it more than I have in this London humidity. It slips easily into pockets and even the cutest of micro bags.” — Jacqueline Kilikita, Beauty Director

“I love styling wands in theory — a compact, travel-friendly way to tame flyaways? Sign me up! In practice, though, many deposit too much product at once, or the product itself is too thick, leaving my hair looking greasy and flat. This one is perfect. It really does feel like a magic wand, smoothing down baby hairs and flyaways with a lightweight serum formula that never leaves a visible residue on my dark brunette hair. It also smells incredible — like a fresh-baked berry pie — which makes every swipe that much more enjoyable. I reach for it most to smooth the halo of flyaways around my hairline and the stubborn ones at the back of my head, making polished hairstyles look effortlessly neat.” — Karina Hoshikawa, Senior Writer
